To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the Danube Fan has experienced at least four major phases of channel avulsion during the Holocene and 2) the youngest leveed channel is controlled by the asymmetry of the levees and the pre-existing topography of the fan.

the recent history of the Danube Fan, and the results are of interest for the understanding of the sedimentation processes on the Danube, the Black Sea and the Mediterranean Sea, which have been influenced by sea level variations during the last 20,000 years.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Danube Fan is a typical turbiditic fan, with a very active channel-levee network and a high rate of channel bifurcation and avulsion, which is probably the result of a complex interplay of tectonic, sedimentary and sea level controls.
the Danube deep sea fan is a complex and active system, which has been shaped by the combined effects of sea level changes, sediment supply, and local bathymetry.

the Danube Fan, as well as other deep-sea fans in semi-enclosed basins, is an excellent model of channel-levee avulsions and of the influence of local topography on the distribution of the sedimentary deposits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the youngest channel-lever system developed during the Neoeuzinian lowstand, the most recent phase was characterized by a succession of channel avulsions with a northward migration, the HARPs are confined by the preexisting topography and the most recent HARPs are the most severely confined.
the Danube Fan has a very complex history of deposition and that the Danube is a very important contributor to the sedimentation in the northwestern Black Sea, even though it is not the only one.
the Danube Fan, as well as the other Black Sea fans, are not passive receivers of terrigenous sediments, but are dynamic depositional systems that are strongly influenced by their own evolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Danube deep sea fan is an excellent analogue to study channel-levee bifurcations and avulsions, which are important for understanding the sedimentary architecture and the evolution of submarine fans in general.
the Danube Fan is a very active and complex depositional system, with a complex internal structure that is poorly known and not fully explained yet.
the Danube Fan, like the Amazon Fan, was a highly active system with a complex evolution during the Holocene.
